title: The NMC Register, 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 (annual data report, UK)
date_evidence: Nursing in Practice dateline '29 Jul 2026' reporting this NMC release; Nursing Times URL slug 'uk-nursing-workforce-more-diverse-but-pipeline-drying-up-29-07-2026'. The PDF carries no publication dateline of its own (a footnote refers to other data 'released on 18 June 2026').
key_claim: In the year to March 2026 the NMC register reached a record 867,935; 30,581 UK-educated professionals joined (4.9% fewer than 32,164) and 10,961 internationally educated professionals joined (9,708, or 47%, fewer); 30,323 left (5.3% more), with retirement among the top three consistent reasons.
frame_summary: The register regulator reports that the register reached a record size but grew more slowly because fewer people joined from both the overseas and UK routes while more left.
verbatim_list: The number of nurses, midwives and nursing associates on the NMC Register has reached a record high of 867,935.
this is 4.9% fewer than the 32,164 who joined the previous year
10,961 professionals who were educated outside the UK joined the NMC Register for the first time. That's 9,708 (47%) fewer than the previous year.
A total of 30,323 people left the NMC Register in the year to March 2026
a 5.3% increase compared to the previous year
(retirement, physical or mental health and burnout or exhaustion)
notes: PDF fetched via WebFetch 04/10/2026; figures re-read in a second pass. title: NHS Vacancy Statistics England, April 2015 - June 2026, Experimental Statistics
key_claim: Registered nursing vacancy rate was 5.3% (23,046 vacancies) at June 2026, down from 6.1% (25,944) a year earlier; whole-workforce rate 6.7% (100,326), down from 7.1%.
frame_summary: NHS England's statistics unit reports that vacancy rates fell year on year across the workforce and in registered nursing to June 2026.
verbatim_quote: The Registered Nursing staff group (which includes midwives and health visitors) had a vacancy rate of 5.3% (23,046 vacancies).
verbatim_list: This is a decrease from the same period the previous year when the vacancy rate was 6.1% (25,944 vacancies).
The workforce as a whole had a vacancy rate of 6.7% (100,326 vacancies).
notes: Key Facts section re-read in order on a second WebFetch pass to confirm which prior-year figure belongs to which staff group (nursing 6.1% / 25,944; whole workforce 7.1% / 105,602). quote_provenance manually-verified (no external egress for the provenance audit).

title: Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026: Why do people come to the UK? Work
key_claim: Health and Care Worker visas fell 45% to 34,143 in the year ending June 2026; visas to nursing professionals fell 95% (22,858 to 1,125) against the year ending December 2023; care-worker visas fell by over 99% (107,772 to 344) after overseas recruitment of care workers ended in July 2025.
frame_summary: The Home Office reports that the Health and Care Worker route has contracted sharply from its 2023 peak, with nursing and care-worker visas close to nil after policy changes.
verbatim_quote: The number of Health and Care Worker visas issued to nursing professionals fell by 95% (22,858 to 1,125) in the YE (year ending) June 2026
verbatim_list: the number of Health and Care Worker visas issued has fallen by 45% to 34,143 in the YE (year ending) June 2026
following the end to overseas recruitment of care workers in July 2025
notes: Page fetched twice via WebFetch 04/10/2026; first attempt at guessed sub-page URLs returned 404 and was discarded; URL here is the one returned by WebSearch. quote_provenance manually-verified.

title: One in four doctors nearing retirement age as WHO warns of global health workforce gap
key_claim: Nearly one in four doctors on average is older than 55 and will retire in the next decade, rising to nearly one in three in high-income countries; projected global shortfall of 11.1 million health workers by 2030; 67 countries will not have enough health workers by 2030.
frame_summary: WHO argues that the global health workforce is growing but ageing, and that a shortfall to 2030 will persist, with retirement exposure highest among doctors in high-income countries.
verbatim_quote: Sixty-seven countries will not have enough health workers to maintain population health needs by 2030.
verbatim_list: Nearly one in four doctors on average is older than 55 and will retire in the next decade
In high-income countries, this increases to nearly one in three.
Projected to reach 11.1 million health workers globally by 2030
notes: Figures concern doctors; the release as fetched carries no equivalent nurse age figure, so the body states that limit explicitly. quote_provenance manually-verified (two WebFetch passes).

title: Getting the next workforce plan right: eight insights from our research
key_claim: Government goal to cut non-UK recruits from 34% to 10% by 2035; non-UK-trained share of new NMC registrants has not once fallen to 10% in 35 years since 1990/91; NHS leaver rate 10.1% in the 12 months to September 2024.
frame_summary: The Health Foundation argues that the NHS's goal of cutting international recruitment to 10% by 2035 has no precedent and needs a far larger domestic pipeline than past plans delivered.
verbatim_quote: has not once fallen to the 10% target in the 35 years since 1990/91
verbatim_list: The government's most recent goal is to reduce the proportion of new recruits from non-UK backgrounds from 34% to 10% by 2035
NHS England reported that 10.1% of hospital and community health service staff left in the 12 months to September 2024
notes: Structural anchor (139 days before scan date): canonical statement of the 2035 self-sufficiency goal and its historical record. quote_provenance manually-verified.

title: UK-educated nurses joining NMC register falls for first time in several years
date_evidence: Nursing in Practice article dateline: 29 Jul 2026 (headline: UK-educated nurses joining NMC register falls for first time in several years)
key_claim: Reports the NMC's year-to-March-2026 data: first fall in five years in UK-educated joiners; register growth 1.7% against 3.3% the year before; NMC says future supply cannot be taken for granted.
frame_summary: A trade-press report arguing that falling UK-educated and overseas joiners together show nurse supply growth slowing, quoting the NMC and the RCN.
verbatim_quote: this marks the first time in five years that the number of new UK-educated professionals joining the register has fallen
verbatim_list: the register grew by only 1.7% compared to 3.3% between April 2024 and March 2025
Together, these findings show a workforce that is larger and more diverse than ever, but one where growth is slowing and future supply cannot be taken for granted.
notes: Secondary reporting of the NMC release; used for the first-fall-in-five-years claim and the NMC's own comment. quote_provenance manually-verified.

title: A-level results day sees fresh call to 'grow supply' of future nurses
date_evidence: Nursing in Practice article dateline: 13 Aug 2026 (headline: A-level results day sees fresh call to grow supply of future nurses)
key_claim: UCAS shows 18,350 accepted onto UK nursing programmes by results day against 18,310 a year earlier; the RCN says numbers have flatlined for four years.
frame_summary: A trade-press report relaying the RCN's argument that nursing course intake has flatlined for four years and the country needs more nurses than are being accepted.
verbatim_quote: Figures show a total of 18,350 students have been accepted to start nursing programmes across the UK
verbatim_list: the 18,310 accepted at this point last year
notes: The article's own wording says 'down slightly on the 18,310', although 18,350 is the larger figure; the body therefore describes the two figures as essentially flat and does not repeat 'down'. quote_provenance manually-verified.

title: Nurses 'stacking shelves' as graduates blocked from third of entry level NHS jobs last month, figures show
key_claim: An RCN Students Committee audit found 33% of Band 5 vacancies advertised in July 2026 required experience that blocked new graduates; an FOI request found advertised Band 5 roles in London fell 68% between 2019-2020 and 2024-2025.
frame_summary: The RCN, a union with a stated position, argues that NHS employers are closing entry-level posts to new graduates under constrained budgets, at odds with the shortage narrative.
verbatim_quote: 33% of Band 5 vacancies, the entry level pay band for registered nurses, advertised in July required experience that blocked new graduates from accessing them
verbatim_list: fell by 68% between academic years 2019-2020 and 2024-2025
Just 26% of jobs advertised (82 out of 317) in England were full time, permanent and open to applicants without professional experience
notes: Advocacy body with a stated position: audit data used directionally and attributed to the RCN in the body. quote_provenance manually-verified.
